items.kind: hygiene (release tooling; S–M) — four faults met at the v0.44.0 cut and fold
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (the integrator, at the v0.44.0 cut); perf-47
items.discussion: the v0.44.0 cut and fold (notes46.md, 2026-10-04/05); M105 S6 (`cut-release.sh`'s perf verdict), `perf_gate.py`, `fold-release.sh`; N145
items.title: the release tooling's four faults at v0.44.0: the cut writes MACHINE PATHS into tracked files; `fold-release.sh` trusts LOCAL main; `ratchet --release` drops bumps without absorbing them; `seal --advance` rewrites the budgets after the verdict's sha
items.body: (1) `cut-release.sh --allow-perf-regression` wrote the verdict file's absolute home path into CHANGELOG's `> Performance:` note, and `perf_gate.py report` wrote the prepared kolt tree's absolute path into `perf/report-vX.Y.Z.md` (twice): `hygiene::no_tracked_file_contains_an_absolute_home_path` would have reddened the release commit; removed by hand. The cut should print names, not paths, and run the hygiene pin on what it wrote before committing. (2) `fold-release.sh` decides 'main already carries the tag' from LOCAL main: the v0.43.0 fold died at `git push origin main`, the resumed run skipped the push, and origin/main sat two releases behind until the v0.44.0 fold. Compare `origin/main` (after a fetch) and push when it lacks the merge; verify origin after the push. (3) `perf_gate.py ratchet --release` resets the `[[bump]]` rows but leaves the bumped rows' ceilings where they were, so an approved bump goes RED at the next release; and `cut-release.sh` never calls the ratchet. At a release, a bumped row's ceiling should become its measured count (the bump absorbed), in the release commit. (4) `seal --advance` (E121's two-green count) rewrites `perf/budgets.toml` AFTER the verdict is written for a sha, leaving the tip without a verdict; the count should live outside the tree, or the advance should be the cut's. Also: the seal's base must be the previous RELEASE built for the reference class - at v0.44.0 the installed toolchain was a dev build and the shipped Linux asset is musl; `perf_gate.py seal` could build or fetch the base itself from the tag. Pins for each.
